environment.note: Paired A/B in one browser session on one clip. Both models are the same 6,291-parameter graph, so this measures whether anything regressed, not which is faster.
environment.limitation: One 20-second run per arm, fixed order, unreplicated, single clip, single machine, numbers transcribed from the diagnostic overlay. Adequate to show that swapping weights changes nothing measurable; not adequate to attribute any difference between the arms.

preRegisteredTargets.dropNote: The candidate arm logged 0 decoder drops and the production arm 10 in the same session. The inference graph is byte-identical, so this is warm-up or session noise and is NOT attributed to the model. Establishing a real difference would need alternating A/B/A/B repetitions with run order recorded.

verdict: Swapping the candidate weights into the production pipeline changes nothing measurable at runtime, which is what an identical inference graph predicts: whole-stage p50 6.34 ms against 6.43, p95 7.40 against 7.44, 38.9% of a 60 Hz budget in both arms, 59.7 presented fps, no budget fallback in either. The pre-registered runtime targets are met. The 10-vs-0 decoder-drop difference is within session noise and is not a property of the weights.
